incident: AA22-320A: Iranian government-sponsored APT actors compromise a Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) network via Log4Shell on VMware Horizon, deploy XMRig, Ngrok, rogue domain admin (intrusion Feb-Jul 2022, advisory 2022-11-16)

sources.title: CISA/FBI Joint CSA AA22-320A: Iranian Government-Sponsored APT Actors Compromise Federal Network, Deploy Crypto Miner, Credential Harvester (2022-11-16)
sources.what_it_gave: entry point (unpatched VMware Horizon server, CVE-2021-44228, Feb 2022), hops (RDP Horizon -> VDI-KMS host; Mimikatz + rogue domain admin; RDP to several hosts with Ngrok; DC compromised), detection (CISA EINSTEIN retrospective analysis April 2022; onsite IR mid-June to mid-July 2022)

narrative_before: In February 2022 likely Iranian government-sponsored actors exploited Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) on an unpatched, internet-facing VMware Horizon server of an FCEB organization; the exploit ran PowerShell that excluded C:\ from Windows Defender, downloaded XMRig crypto-mining files and created a scheduled task running as SYSTEM, using a VMware service account with administrator and system-level access (AA22-320A). The actors then used RDP with the built-in DefaultAccount to move from the Horizon server to a VMware VDI-KMS host, where they downloaded ~30 MB of tools (PsExec, Mimikatz, Ngrok) from transfer.sh, ran Mimikatz, and created a rogue domain administrator account. With that account they RDP'd into several hosts, manually disabled Windows Defender on each, implanted Ngrok reverse proxies for persistence/C2, changed local administrator passwords as a fallback, and compromised the domain controller (get-adcomputer enumeration); an attempted LSASS dump through Task Manager was blocked by antivirus. In April 2022 CISA's EINSTEIN intrusion detection system showed bidirectional traffic between the agency and 51.89.181[.]64 (a known Log4Shell exploitation IP) with a suspected LDAP callback over 443, which CISA judged a confirmed compromise; CISA performed onsite incident response from mid-June to mid-July 2022 and confirmed the DC compromise (AA22-320A).

detection_moments.description: Initial exploitation, February 2022: Log4Shell on the Horizon server, XMRig deployed, scheduled task persistence, Defender exclusion. Not detected by the agency.
detection_moments.evidence: 'In February 2022, the actors exploited Log4Shell for initial access to the organization's unpatched VMware Horizon server... the exploit ran a PowerShell command that added a Windows Defender exclusion for the entire C:\ drive... downloaded... XMRig' - AA22-320A

detection_moments.description: April 2022: CISA EINSTEIN retrospective analysis shows bidirectional traffic to 51.89.181[.]64 and a suspected LDAP callback on 443 - CISA informs the agency ('confirmed compromise'). By then the Horizon server was compromised and CISA already suspected the DC was compromised from third-party reporting; the Mimikatz/rogue-DA activity on VDI-KMS precedes the DC and Ngrok hosts. Exact dates of the hops are not given.
detection_moments.evidence: 'In April 2022, CISA conducted retrospective analysis using EINSTEIN... identified suspected APT activity... bidirectional traffic between the network and a known malicious IP address 51.89.181[.]64... the traffic indicated a confirmed compromise' and 'CISA suspected DC compromise based on third-party reporting' - AA22-320A

detection_moments.description: Mid-June to mid-July 2022: CISA onsite incident response confirms the full scope - rogue domain admin, Ngrok implants on several hosts, DC compromise, changed local admin passwords.
detection_moments.evidence: 'From mid-June through mid-July 2022, CISA conducted an incident response engagement... confirmed... the actors moved laterally to the domain controller... implanted Ngrok reverse proxies on several hosts to maintain persistence' - AA22-320A

'Several hosts' with Ngrok: count unknown; modelled as 3 (rule 1 allows 3-10).
No business services are named as disrupted; services listed are the directory and the VDI platform at risk (DC compromise). Values assigned by rule 4, flagged.
Exact dates of lateral movement between Feb and Apr 2022 are not given; m2 alert set assumes VDI-KMS and DC were compromised by April (CISA already suspected DC compromise then).
